The research findings were disseminated and plans on how to support each country in addressing the legal and policy gaps was drafted. Capacity-building training in I-engej was already done in 2022 with WROs and As across the region. Similarly, in the Somalia region, Musawah engaged the coalition members in the interpretation of Quranic laws.

As a strategic partner, Musawah would support the capacity strengthening of WROs/As, particularly in family law, through research, training, and creating regional platforms of engagement in family law.

Year one Musawah focused on country-level mapping of Muslim family laws, policies, and practices in Ethiopia, South Sudan, Sudan, Uganda, and Somaliland to identify legal and policy gaps and advocacy priorities and needs with regards to family law in each country. This was completed by December 2021.
Musawah will continue to support advocacy on family law across the region.

The efforts of Musawah have affected a wide range of laws, rules, and policies concerning Muslim family law reform. Their thorough investigation of Muslim family laws and practices in Uganda, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Sudan, Somalia, and Somaliland by 2021 will help to shape advocacy campaigns. After the completion of a comparative study spanning all project nations in 2022, further reform initiatives will be guided. Musawah shared its results widely into 2023 to improve regional exposure and involve stakeholders via newsletters and focused interactions with reporters. Using comprehensive site visits and interaction with more than forty national groups and activists, Musawah has also deepened its awareness of local issues and approaches, therefore promoting successful cooperation to further family law changes.

Musawah is a strategic partner, supporting all the WCW implementation partners, particularly to advance family law in the region. Musawah has been aggressively developing their ability to help members of four consortium partners—NAGAAD, SIHA-Sudan, SIHA South Sudan, and EWLA Ethiopia—assume transforming leadership roles. Musawah teamed with NAGAAD in September 2021 to provide 30 national women's rights activists and groups from Mogadishu and Hargeisa—including members of the NAGAAD team—a hybrid capacity-building program. This program concentrated on the variety of Qur'anic readings, juristic viewpoints, and conceptual tools required for gender transformation in Muslim family law and practices. Under IWILAP, Musawah participated in CEDAW shadow reporting in Uganda, offering follow-up engagement and capacity support, including knowledge-building virtual calls, in partnership with the Muslim Center for Justice and Law (MCJL). Working with FIDA-Uganda, Musawah hosted a knowledge-building session for Ugandan lawyers on the rights of women under Islam and Muslim law in 2023, therefore benefiting thirty participants—27 women and three males. These initiatives have enabled groups of women's rights activists and leaders to assume transforming leadership responsibilities.
5 per country
